tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List the person's Leash apps (id, slug, allowed origins).

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create a Leash app: its own walled-off Postgres schema and sign-in. slug: 2–40 chars, lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. origins: where the web app is served (needed for browser sign-in and CORS). Free plans allow 1 app, Pro 25.

tools.name: set_app_origins
tools.description: Replace the app's allowed web origins (sign-in return URLs and CORS). Each is https://host[:port] or http://localhost:port, no path; at most 10.

tools.name: usage
tools.description: Show the account's storage: bytes per app as last measured (null with a note until first measured, a few minutes after the first write), total vs the plan's limit, plan, whether writes are blocked for being over the limit, snapshot usage, and the database server's state (running/stopped: it sleeps w

tools.name: reclaim_space
tools.description: Compact the app's tables that have many deleted rows (VACUUM FULL), then re-measure storage. Use after deleting lots of data to get back under the storage limit. Returns the tables compacted, the tables skipped because the app's role doesn't own them, and whether writes are still blocked.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the app's tables and views (name, kind, estimated row count).

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Describe one of the app's tables or views: columns (name, type, nullable, default), primary key, constraints, indexes, and a view's definition.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL SELECT against the app's tables (its own schema). Returns { columns, rows (arrays), truncated }: at most 1000 rows and 10 MB; int8/numeric come back as strings, bytea as base64, dates as ISO text. Writes, multiple statements and system functions are refused.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Run one SQL statement that changes data (insert/update/delete) or the schema. Returns { rowCount, columns, rows, rowsTruncated, snapshots }, or for DDL { changeId, snapshots } (logged like apply_schema_change). At most 100 RETURNING rows (10 MB) come back: when rowsTruncated is true the write still

tools.name: apply_schema_change
tools.description: Apply one schema change (create/alter/drop table, index, view, sequence; truncate) to the app's own schema, recorded in its change log with your description. Destructive changes (drop table/column, column type change, truncate) first save a 7-day snapshot of each affected table; if the snapshot cap

tools.name: mint_device_key
tools.description: Mint a device key for a non-browser client of the app (script, extension, phone app). The key is returned ONCE: store it in the device's local config or secret store, never in browser code or a repo. Use it as Authorization: Bearer lk_… on the data API.

tools.name: list_device_keys
tools.description: List the app's device keys (id, name, created, last used, revoked). Never shows the keys themselves.

tools.name: revoke_device_key
tools.description: Revoke one of the app's device keys (it stops working immediately).

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List the app's safety snapshots (taken automatically before destructive changes; kept 7 days), newest first.

tools.name: restore_snapshot
tools.description: Restore a snapshot as a table in the app: under its original name if that table no longer exists, otherwise as <table>_restored_<timestamp>, or as asTable. Rows only: re-create constraints, indexes and defaults with apply_schema_change. Returns { table }.

tools.name: get_direct_connection
tools.description: Pro only: a Postgres connection locked to the app's own schema, for apps with their own server (Drizzle, migrations). Keep it in the server's environment, never in browser code.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "query" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "execute" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "mint_device_key" references sensitive artifacts (secret, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
